pick.headline: Thatcher wins a third term
pick.summary: In the British general election of June 11, 1987, Margaret Thatcher's Conservatives won a third consecutive victory, with a reduced but still large majority over Neil Kinnock's Labor Party.
pick.significance: Thatcher's third term kept Reagan's closest ally in power through the end of the Cold War. In Buenos Aires the vote was watched for what it meant for the Falklands/Malvinas: Labor had been seen as more open to talks.
pick.fbis: The Latin America report of June 12, 1987, carried Argentine reaction on election day: a Radical senator said Buenos Aires would negotiate over the Malvinas if Labor won, but expected a Thatcher victory, perhaps with a majority small enough to force talks on sovereignty.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: Latin America, No. 113, 12 June 1987
evidence.snippet: …tina's attitude towards the Malvinas was best described as “active patience". Gass said if the Labour Party wins today's elections in Britain, the Argentine Government would sit down to negotiations. He added a Margaret Thatcher victory was the more likely outcome but a reduced majority might force the Conservatives to respect United Nations resolutions and discuss sovereignty.
